subject.title: [Bug]: Browser interactions can exhaust model context by injecting too much page content

question: Should OpenClaw change browser interaction semantics toward compact default reads and post-action change reports, and if so should that be default behavior or an opt-in browser snapshot/action mode?
rationale: Current code already has caps and efficient mode, but the requested fix changes model-facing browser semantics and compatibility with full snapshot workflows; automation should not choose that product boundary alone.

options.title: Add compact default contract
options.body: Make interactive browser reads and action results compact by default while preserving explicit full/raw snapshot modes for existing workflows.

options.title: Add opt-in compact mode
options.body: Keep current defaults and add a new documented compact/action-diff mode that agents or configs can choose when context pressure matters.

options.title: Keep current safeguards
options.body: Treat the 40k cap, optional efficient mode, and skill guidance as sufficient, leaving richer goal-shaped reads to future plugin or product work.

recommendation.title: Add compact default contract
recommendation.body: Make interactive browser reads and action results compact by default while preserving explicit full/raw snapshot modes for existing workflows.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is about browser plugin public behavior and docs, and recent history points to steipete as the strongest browser product-boundary owner among the likely owners.
